access-panel.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 door controller: a PN532 NFC reader on I2C for fobs/cards/phone tags, a Wiegand keypad on GPIO32/GPIO33 for PIN entry, a servo-driven latch on GPIO13 and a relay output for the strike plate.
access-panel.name: Door access panel (NFC + keypad + servo latch)

requirements.text: scan NFC tags and forward UIDs to Home Assistant's tag registry
accept PIN entry from the Wiegand keypad
actuate the latch servo and strike relay

warnings.text: Most Wiegand readers idle D0/D1 at 5V. Add resistor dividers or a level shifter before GPIO32/GPIO33 unless the reader is confirmed 3.3V-safe.

actuator-harness.description: A brake or valve actuator on one 8-way cable: reversible motor on a discrete MOSFET bridge, feedback pot on an ADC pin, tach switch on a pulse counter. The harness connector's positions are passthroughs landing on the bridge's output nodes, the pot and tach roles, and the rails; a 4-way panel pigtail carries an encoder and a button the same way.
actuator-harness.name: Actuator harness

air-quality-station.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 with the current-generation Sensirion stack on I2C (SCD4x true CO2, SHT4x temp/RH, SGP4x VOC index, VEML7700 lux, BME680 pressure/gas) and a Plantower PMS5003 particulate sensor on UART2.
air-quality-station.name: Indoor air quality station

requirements.text: publish CO2, PM2.5, VOC index, temperature, humidity, pressure and illuminance
all I2C sensors share one bus; addresses must not collide

warnings.text: The SCD4x pulls ~200mA bursts during measurement; the 10uF bulk cap near its VCC matters on long supply runs.

analog-node.description: ESP32-DevKitC with an ADS1115 4-channel 16-bit I2C ADC providing two readings (single-ended panel voltage on A0, differential shunt current on A2/A3) plus a board ADC1 pin reading the 3V3 rail through a divider. Demonstrates rescuing analog headroom from ESP32's narrow built-in ADC.
analog-node.name: Analog measurement node (ADS1115 + onboard ADC)

requirements.text: report two external analog channels at 16-bit resolution via an ADS1115
report the onboard 3V3 rail voltage via the ESP32's built-in ADC
external ADC must coexist with WiFi -- avoid ADC2 pins

atom-echo.description: Minimal M5Stack Atom Echo device: the onboard SK6812 RGB status LED on GPIO27 driven via the ESP32 RMT peripheral, plus the programmable front button on GPIO39. A starting point for an Echo-based controller before adding the I2S mic/speaker.
atom-echo.name: M5Stack Atom Echo (LED + button)

requirements.text: show status on the onboard RGB LED
read the programmable front button

atom-lite.description: M5Stack Atom Lite with its onboard SK6812 RGB LED, the front button, and the I2S PDM microphone auto-populated.
atom-lite.name: M5Stack Atom Lite (onboard)

requirements.text: expose the board's built-in peripherals

atom-matrix.description: M5Stack Atom Matrix driving its onboard 5x5 (25-LED) SK6812 RGB matrix on GPIO27 via the ESP32 RMT peripheral, plus the programmable button on GPIO39 hidden under the matrix.
atom-matrix.name: M5Stack Atom Matrix (5x5 LED + button)

requirements.text: drive the onboard 5x5 RGB LED matrix
read the programmable button

atoms3-lcd.description: M5Stack AtomS3 driving a 20x4 HD44780 character LCD over its Grove I2C port via a PCF8574 backpack. The tiny S3 cube sits behind the panel and renders status text on the big, readable character display -- a cheap always-on status board.
atoms3-lcd.name: AtomS3 character-LCD status panel

requirements.text: render status text on a 20x4 character LCD
LCD is 5V HD44780 on a PCF8574 backpack; drive it from the AtomS3 Grove I2C port (GPIO1/GPIO2)

warnings.text: The PCF8574 backpack pulls SDA/SCL to its 5V VCC, but the ESP32-S3 GPIOs are not 5V-tolerant. Most Grove LCD units work in practice because I2C is open-drain and the bus rarely swings to a hard 5V, but for a clean design add a level shifter or pull the bus to 3V3.

atoms3-lite.description: Minimal M5Stack AtomS3 Lite (ESP32-S3) device: the onboard WS2812C RGB status LED on GPIO35 driven via the ESP32 RMT peripheral, plus the programmable button on GPIO41.
atoms3-lite.name: M5Stack AtomS3 Lite (LED + button)

requirements.text: show status on the onboard RGB LED
read the programmable button

atoms3-onboard.description: M5Stack AtomS3 with its built-in parts pre-placed: the 0.85" 128x128 ST7789 LCD on the internal SPI bus, the programmable front button, and the MPU6886 6-axis IMU on I2C. This is exactly what the studio auto-populates when you pick or USB-detect an AtomS3.
atoms3-onboard.name: M5Stack AtomS3 (onboard peripherals)

requirements.text: drive the onboard 0.85" ST7789 LCD
read the onboard MPU6886 IMU + the front button

atomu.description: Minimal M5Stack AtomU device: the onboard SK6812 RGB status LED on GPIO27 driven via the ESP32 RMT peripheral, plus the programmable button on GPIO39. The USB-A stick form factor before adding the PDM mic or IR.
atomu.name: M5Stack AtomU (LED + button)

requirements.text: show status on the onboard RGB LED
read the programmable button

atomu-onboard.description: M5Stack AtomU (USB-A stick) with its onboard parts pre-placed: SK6812 RGB LED, the button, the IR transmitter, and the SPM1423 PDM microphone -- the full onboard set the studio auto-populates.
atomu-onboard.name: M5Stack AtomU (onboard)

requirements.text: expose the AtomU's built-in LED, button, IR, and mic

attic-logger.description: WeMos D1 Mini logging temperature/humidity from a DHT22 on a GPIO and barometric pressure from an older BMP180 on I2C -- a 'parts box' build pairing the single-wire DHT protocol with a legacy I2C barometer people already have on hand.
attic-logger.name: Attic climate logger (legacy parts)

requirements.text: report attic temperature + humidity from a DHT22
report barometric pressure from a legacy BMP180
DHT22 is single-wire (one GPIO); BMP180 is I2C-only at the fixed 0x77 address

awning-control.description: ESP8266 D1 Mini drives a motorized retractable deck awning via H-bridge PWM, with limit switches and manual buttons read through an MCP23008 I2C port expander. Sensors and switches are now modeled as gpio_input/gpio_output components with expander_pin connections; PWM outputs and the cover platform stay in esphome_extras.
awning-control.name: Deck awning controller

requirements.text: open/close motorized awning via cover entity
two physical buttons toggle in/out
two limit switches stop the motor at endstops
8 GPIO needed; expand via MCP23008 to keep native pins for PWM

warnings.text: PWM motor drivers (esp8266_pwm on D5/D6) and the endstop cover platform live in esphome_extras until library entries for those land.

bench-io.description: The discrete building blocks on one board: a status LED, an NPN driver for a 5 V relay coil, a logic-level MOSFET driver for a 12 V fan on PWM, a divider to read the 12 V supply, and a level shifter for a 5 V 1-Wire line.
bench-io.name: Bench I/O board

bl0906-mainmeter.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 reading a BL0906 6-channel energy meter (Athom EM6-style) over UART2. Six CT clamps land on channels 1-6; the chip aggregates total power and total energy across all of them.
bl0906-mainmeter.name: BL0906 6-channel mains energy monitor

requirements.text: publish per-channel current/power/energy from six 2000:1 CT clamps
publish global voltage / frequency / total power / total energy

blind-stepper.description: A 28BYJ-48 geared stepper on a ULN2003 driver, USB powered.
blind-stepper.name: Motorized blind (28BYJ-48)

requirements.text: open and close a window blind
USB 5V powered (the 28BYJ-48 draws up to ~240 mA)

bluemotion.description: ESP8266 D1 Mini, single PIR on GPIO4, single WS2812B on GPIO14. Motion lights the LED; LED also blinks on boot.
bluemotion.name: Blue motion sensor with NeoPixel feedback

requirements.text: report motion as a binary_sensor
single-LED visual feedback on motion + boot

bluesonoff.description: Sonoff Basic (ESP-01S, 1MB flash). Single GPIO button (boot strap pin) toggles a single GPIO relay. Status LED on GPIO13.
bluesonoff.name: Sonoff Basic relay (soffit outlets)

requirements.text: expose mains relay as a switch in HA
front button toggles the relay locally
status LED reflects ESPHome health

warnings.text: GPIO0 is a strap pin (must be HIGH at boot to enter normal mode). Sonoff Basic ties it through the front button to 3V3 with a pull-up; pressing the button at boot WILL force flash mode. Acceptable on a deployed device, but not flexible.
ESPHome's status_led is a singleton platform with no library entry yet -- lives in esphome_extras.

button-toggles-light.description: Phase 1 worked example for intent-to-device synthesis: one GPIO button toggles one GPIO switch (relay/LED/mosfet). The trigger -> action wiring lives in `automations` (not as a raw `params.on_press` blob), so the generator lowers it from the library's `capability` blocks into ESPHome's `on_press: [{switch.toggle: porch_light}]`.
button-toggles-light.name: Porch button toggles porch light

requirements.text: press button to toggle the porch light

c3-supermini.description: ESP32-C3 SuperMini with its onboard parts pre-placed: the addressable status LED and the BOOT button.
c3-supermini.name: ESP32-C3 SuperMini (onboard)

requirements.text: expose the board's built-in peripherals

c6-supermini.description: ESP32-C6 SuperMini with its onboard WS2812 status LED and BOOT button auto-populated.
c6-supermini.name: ESP32-C6 SuperMini (onboard)

requirements.text: expose the board's built-in peripherals

co2-display.description: Wemos D1 Mini with an MH-Z19 NDIR CO2 sensor on a software UART (D6/D5), a TM1637 4-digit display (D1/D2) bound to the CO2 value via the show intent, and a piezo buzzer (D7) that plays the named alarm melody when CO2 crosses 1200ppm.
co2-display.name: CO2 monitor with 7-segment readout

requirements.text: publish CO2 ppm and show it on the local display

warnings.text: MH-Z19 needs ~3 minutes of warm-up after power-on before readings settle.

desk-climate.description: ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1 with a Sensirion SHT3x temperature/humidity sensor. Demonstrates the modern precision-sensor option (vs the AHT20 budget pick in room-climate.json).
desk-climate.name: Desk climate (Sensirion)

requirements.text: publish desk temperature + humidity at 30s intervals
use precision-grade sensing (Sensirion ±0.3°C / ±2% RH)

desk-matrix.description: ESP32-DevKitC driving an 8x8 (64 LEDs) WS2812 matrix via the chip's RMT peripheral. Strictly preferred over the bit-banged neopixelbus driver on ESP32 hardware: doesn't disable interrupts, doesn't fight WiFi, hits frame rates the bit-banger can't.
desk-matrix.name: Desk LED matrix (ESP32 RMT-driven WS2812)

passives.purpose: series resistor on data line; tames overshoot at the first pixel

requirements.text: drive 64 WS2812 LEDs at full frame rate
use ESP32 RMT (not bit-banged neopixelbus) so WiFi + LED rendering coexist cleanly
8x8 matrix at full white peaks at ~3.8A; budget the supply accordingly

distance-sensor.description: ESP8266 NodeMCU v2 with an HC-SR04 (D5/D6) and a single WS2812B (D1) whose color is driven by the measured distance.
distance-sensor.name: Ultrasonic distance sensor with NeoPixel feedback

requirements.text: publish ultrasonic distance as a sensor
color a NeoPixel red→green based on measured distance

warnings.text: HC-SR04 ECHO is 5V; add a voltage divider to ESP8266 GPIO or use HC-SR04P.

encoder-drives-stepper.description: Phase-2 worked example for intent-to-device synthesis: a rotary encoder's cumulative value drives a ULN2003/28BYJ-48 stepper. The encoder's on_value (kind=value) trigger fires stepper.set_target through a transform lowered to an ESPHome !lambda -- target = (long)(x * 10), so each encoder detent commands ten motor steps. This is the value->transform->action case that complements the declarative event->action examples (button-toggles-light, motion-turns-on-light).
encoder-drives-stepper.name: Knob drives a stepper (value -> transform -> action)

requirements.text: turn the knob and the motor follows

energy-monitor.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 measuring mains power three ways: a PZEM-004T v3 over Modbus/UART2 for real power on one circuit, an SCT-013 CT clamp on GPIO34 for a second circuit's current, and an INA219 on I2C watching a 12V DC rail.
energy-monitor.name: Whole-circuit energy monitor

requirements.text: publish real power, energy and power factor for the monitored AC circuit
publish RMS current from a clamp-on CT without breaking the conductor
publish voltage/current/power of the 12V DC accessory rail

warnings.text: The PZEM-004T measurement side connects to live mains: enclose it, fuse the voltage tap, and keep the TTL side's optocoupled isolation intact.

esp32-audio.description: ESP32 NodeMCU-32S, Arduino framework. MAX98357A I2S DAC drives a Class-D speaker; ST7789V SPI display shows a clock + status. Hardware mute and backlight switches.
esp32-audio.name: Garage I2S audio + ST7789 dashboard

requirements.text: act as a media_player streaming I2S audio to an external Class-D amp
render a clock + status on a 240x320 ST7789 dashboard
physical mute switch + backlight switch
Arduino framework (max98357a media_player is arduino-only in upstream ESPHome; revisit when esp-idf adds the platform)

warnings.text: font definitions, color palette, status_led, time, and the system status binary_sensor live in esphome_extras.

esp32cam.description: AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM (OV2640) wired to the board's fixed camera pinout -- the standard parallel DVP camera bus (8 data lines + XCLK/PCLK/VSYNC/HREF) plus the SCCB control I2C. Streams over the built-in camera web server.
esp32cam.name: AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM

requirements.text: stream the OV2640 camera over the ESP32 camera web server
camera pins are fixed by the AI-Thinker board layout

warnings.text: The OV2640 DVP pins are hardwired on the AI-Thinker module; they're not reassignable. GPIO0 doubles as the camera XCLK and the boot-strap pin, so hold it low only for flashing.

esp32cam-wrover.description: Freenove-style ESP32-WROVER-CAM (OV2640) on the WROVER camera pinout -- XCLK on GPIO32 and the SCCB I2C on GPIO13/12, which (unlike the AI-Thinker) frees GPIO26/27 for IO. Streams over the camera web server.
esp32cam-wrover.name: ESP32-WROVER-CAM (Freenove)

requirements.text: stream the OV2640 camera over the ESP32 camera web server
WROVER camera pinout: XCLK on GPIO32, SCCB I2C on GPIO13/12

warnings.text: WROVER-CAM camera pins are hardwired to the module; GPIO12/14/15 are boot-strap pins, so the camera must be idle at reset.

flow-meter.description: ESP32-DevKitC counting pulses from a flow/tachometer sensor, an APA102 (DotStar) RGB strip for status, and a piezo buzzer playing RTTTL alerts. A water-flow / RPM monitor with visual + audible feedback.
flow-meter.name: Pulse flow meter + DotStar + buzzer

requirements.text: count pulses from a flow / tachometer sensor
show status on an APA102 DotStar strip
play RTTTL alert tones on a piezo buzzer
detect motion at front door
outdoor, covered
USB powered

grill-probe.description: ESP32-DevKitC reading a K-type thermocouple through a MAX31855 SPI amplifier (read-only, no MOSI line) and an MPU6050 6-axis IMU on I2C used as a lid open/close detector. The thermocouple covers smoker/kiln range; the IMU's accelerometer tells you when someone opens the grill.
grill-probe.name: Grill probe (MAX31855 thermocouple + MPU6050 lid sensor)

requirements.text: report grill temperature from a K-type thermocouple via MAX31855
report lid orientation + vibration from an MPU6050
MAX31855 is read-only SPI (CLK/MISO/CS only) -- no MOSI line required

guarded-button-light.description: Phase-5 worked example for intent-to-device synthesis: a button press toggles a light, BUT only when an enable switch is on (a manual override / safety interlock). Exercises condition gating -- the trigger fires AND every condition in the list must hold. The generator wraps the action list in `if: { condition: { switch.is_on: enable }, then: [switch.toggle: light] }`. Pairing the button-toggles-light shape with a single is_on condition is the simplest demonstration that composition between the trigger graph and the condition graph works without touching either side.
guarded-button-light.name: Button toggles a light only when the enable switch is on

requirements.text: toggle the light when the button is pressed AND the enable switch is on

heltec-v4-gnss-tracker.description: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4 with its SH1.25-8 GNSS module (L76K, 9600 baud), uplinking latitude/longitude/satellites over LoRaWAN via lorawan-for-esphome. Field order matches the wirestudio-esphome-us915-sub2-gnss ChirpStack profile codec. Bench-validated 2026-08-30: module TX is GPIO39 (MCU rx), module RX GPIO38; power-up order VEXT(36 low) -> EN(34 low) -> RST(42 high) -> STANDBY/wake(40 high), ~1 s warmup. An undriven standby leaves the module mute with TX held low.
heltec-v4-gnss-tracker.name: Heltec V4 GNSS tracker

requirements.text: uplink GNSS position over LoRaWAN

keypad.description: WeMos D1 Mini reads eight buttons through a PCF8574 I2C GPIO expander. Validates the studio's expander_pin_key fallback path (no override; key matches library_id).
keypad.name: 8-button keypad via PCF8574

requirements.text: report eight independent button states as binary_sensors
single I2C bus -- no extra GPIOs consumed per button

params.lambda_:
it.printf(0, 0, id(font1), "Weight");
it.printf(0, 24, id(font2), "%.0f g", id(scale).state);

kitchen-scale.description: WeMos D1 Mini reading a load cell through an HX711 24-bit ADC and displaying grams on a 128x64 SSD1306 OLED. The HX711's 2-wire serial (DOUT/SCK) is bit-banged on two GPIOs; the OLED shares an I2C bus on the standard D1/D2 pins.
kitchen-scale.name: Kitchen scale (HX711 + OLED readout)

passives.purpose: bulk decoupling for the load-cell front-end

requirements.text: report weight in grams from a load cell via HX711
show the live weight on a small OLED
HX711 protocol is custom 2-wire serial -- not I2C, not SPI

led-display.description: ESP32-DevKitC driving a MAX7219 8x8 LED matrix over SPI and a TM1638 LED&KEY module (8 seven-segment digits + 8 LEDs + 8 buttons) over its own 3-wire interface. Two cheap numeric/segment displays on one board.
led-display.name: MAX7219 matrix + TM1638 module

requirements.text: drive a MAX7219 8x8 LED matrix over SPI
drive a TM1638 7-segment + LED + key module

lorawan-battery-uplink.description: W2 worked example for the LoRaWAN external-component path: a TTGO LoRa32 v1 reads its battery voltage via the ADC and uplinks it through `lorawan-for-esphome` to a US915 sub-band 2 gateway. The smallest design that exercises the full new path -- external_components fetch, lorawan: block, payload sensor binding -- so the generator output can be gated by `esphome config` in CI and hand-flashed against the live ChirpStack for the spike's hardware-join test. Keys ride `fleet.secrets_ref` -> `!secret` references; the actual values are minted by the ChirpStack provision step (W3) and written to secrets.yaml. The standalone Arduino path is untouched.
lorawan-battery-uplink.name: TTGO LoRa32 v1 battery uplink (lorawan-for-esphome spike)

requirements.text: uplink battery voltage to ChirpStack via LoRaWAN

motion-turns-on-light.description: Second phase-1 worked example: a PIR motion sensor triggers a WS2812B LED to turn on. Exercises a different capability pair than button-toggles-light (sensor event -> light action vs. input event -> switch action), proving the lowering generalises across categories. The motion sensor's on_press event lowers to `light.turn_on: porch_light`; on_release lowers to `light.turn_off`.
motion-turns-on-light.name: Motion turns on the porch light

requirements.text: turn on the porch light when motion is detected

motor-position.description: Discrete MOSFET H-bridge driving a small 5 V gearmotor, with the actuator's feedback potentiometer on an ADC pin. The bridge is exposed as two plain outputs for a position loop to drive.
motor-position.name: Motor position controller

multi-temp.description: ESP8266 D1 Mini with two DS18B20 1-wire sensors sharing a single GPIO bus. Demonstrates the 1-wire bus type and the per-sensor ROM addressing pattern. Adds an RCWL-0516 microwave motion sensor on a separate GPIO so the controller can suppress polling when the room is empty.
multi-temp.name: Multi-zone DS18B20 temperatures

requirements.text: two temperature readings on a single bus
occupancy hint via microwave radar

nextion-thermostat.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 with a Nextion HMI display on UART2 (GPIO16/GPIO17 @ 9600 baud) and an SHT3xD temp/humidity sensor on the board's default I2C. The Nextion's GUI is uploaded separately via the Nextion Editor; this design just feeds it sensor values.
nextion-thermostat.name: Nextion HMI thermostat panel

requirements.text: drive a Nextion 2.4"-3.5" HMI display over UART for thermostat UI
publish room temperature + humidity from an SHT3xD

warnings.text: The Nextion's VCC rides the board's 5V rail (USB) -- a Nextion at full backlight pulls 200-250mA. Check your USB supply margin or feed the display from a separate 5V brick if you're also driving WS2812 strips off the same regulator.

oled.description: ESP8266 D1 Mini driving an SSD1306 128x64 I2C OLED with reset on D0. Shows time, date, and the device IP.
oled.name: Status OLED

requirements.text: render time, date, and IP on a 128x64 OLED
publish uptime and wifi_signal sensors

oled-knob.description: The 1.3-inch SH1106 white OLED + EC11 rotary-encoder combo module, the kind sold as one board for menu UIs. The SH1106 display rides the I2C bus; the EC11's quadrature A/B feed the rotary_encoder sensor and its push-switch is a separate gpio_input button. The module also carries two auxiliary push buttons, each wired as its own gpio_input binary sensor.
oled-knob.name: OLED + rotary-knob control panel

requirements.text: render a menu UI on the 1.3-inch OLED
scroll the menu with the rotary encoder
select with the encoder's push button
read the two auxiliary push buttons

output-hub.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 driving banks of outputs without spending MCU pins: a PCA9685 on I2C provides two dimmable 12-bit PWM channels, and an SN74HC595 shift register (GPIO25/26/27) fans out a relay-module output on its pin 0.
output-hub.name: PWM + shift-register output hub

requirements.text: expose two dimmable LED channels from the PCA9685
switch a relay through the shift register without using an MCU pin

warnings.text: Shift-register outputs float until the first latch after boot; wire OE with a pull-up if the relay must stay off through reset.

parking-distance.description: NodeMCU v2 + VL53L0X laser ToF rangefinder. Strictly better than the HC-SR04 ultrasonic for indoor parking-spot use: tighter beam, no acoustic-reflection issues, no 5V level on the signal lines.
parking-distance.name: Parking distance (laser ToF)

requirements.text: publish indoor distance to ~1.2m with mm-level resolution
report a 'too close' binary state below a threshold
no 5V level shifters

presence-media-node.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 media-room node: an LD2410 mmWave sensor on UART2 (256000 baud) for still-presence detection, and a TSOP38238 IR receiver on GPIO25 to learn and react to remote-control codes.
presence-media-node.name: mmWave presence + IR remote receiver

requirements.text: detect still presence (couch occupancy) for media-room automations
receive and decode IR remote codes

warnings.text: Mount the LD2410 with clear line of sight; it detects through plastic but not metal. Ceiling or high-wall placement reads the room best.

presence-rf.description: ESP32-DevKitC with a Hi-Link LD2420 24GHz mmWave presence sensor on one UART and a Sonoff-style 433MHz RF bridge (EFM8) on a second UART. Room presence plus relaying cheap 433MHz remotes/sensors into Home Assistant.
presence-rf.name: mmWave presence + 433MHz RF bridge

requirements.text: report room presence from an LD2420 mmWave sensor (UART)
receive/transmit 433MHz codes via an RF bridge (UART)
two UART peripherals -> two of the ESP32's hardware UARTs

rc522.description: ESP8266 D1 Mini with an MFRC522 RFID reader on SPI, plus a NeoPixel status LED, a piezo buzzer driven by RTTTL, and a hardware button.
rc522.name: RC522 RFID reader station

requirements.text: scan RFID tags via MFRC522 over SPI
feedback on tag scan: NeoPixel flash + RTTTL beep, both maskable from HA
physical button for manual interaction

warnings.text: Piezo buzzer (esp8266_pwm output) and RTTTL block live in esphome_extras until a buzzer/rtttl library entry lands.

room-climate.description: WeMos D1 Mini with a BH1750 ambient-light sensor and an AHT20 temperature/humidity sensor sharing one I2C bus. Demonstrates the cheap multi-sensor pattern that ships on most AliExpress weather modules.
room-climate.name: Room climate (light + AHT20)

requirements.text: report room illuminance in lux
report room temperature + humidity
single shared I2C bus -- no extra GPIOs

rs485-energy.description: ESP32-DevKitC-V4 reading an Eastron SDM230 energy meter over Modbus RTU. UART2 (GPIO16/GPIO17) drives a MAX485 transceiver; GPIO5 toggles the transceiver's combined DE+RE direction pin. The studio's modbus component owns the protocol layer, sdm_meter rides on top.
rs485-energy.name: Eastron SDM230 single-phase energy meter via RS485

requirements.text: publish per-phase voltage / current / power and total import/export energy from an SDM230
RS485 is half-duplex through a MAX485; flow_control_pin must drive DE+RE in lockstep

warnings.text: Wire UART RX/TX through a MAX485 (or equivalent) transceiver: A/B to the SDM230 terminals 9/10, RO/DI to GPIO16/GPIO17, DE+RE tied together to GPIO5.

s3-devkitc.description: Espressif ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 with its onboard WS2812 RGB LED (GPIO48) and BOOT button.
s3-devkitc.name: ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 (onboard)

requirements.text: expose the board's built-in peripherals

s3-supermini.description: ESP32-S3 SuperMini with its onboard WS2812 RGB LED and BOOT button.
s3-supermini.name: ESP32-S3 SuperMini (onboard)

requirements.text: expose the board's built-in peripherals

securitypanel.description: ESP8266 D1 Mini reads 12 contact + motion sensors through an MCP23017 over I2C and drives a piezo buzzer (RTTTL) on D7. Each sensor pin is its own gpio_input component bound to an expander_pin connection.
securitypanel.name: Whole-house door/window/motion security panel

requirements.text: publish 11 door/window/motion binary_sensors to Home Assistant
play short RTTTL tones on sensor events and a longer one on API connect
drive a security siren as a switch
16 GPIOs needed; expand via MCP23017

smart-plug.description: ESP8285 1MB module wired the way Athom / Sonoff Basic R3+ smart plugs are: GPIO12 drives the relay coil, GPIO13 is the active-low status LED, GPIO0 is the front button, and the CSE7766 streams AC voltage/current/power/energy into UART RX (GPIO3) at 4800 8E1.
smart-plug.name: Athom-style smart plug (CSE7766 power metering)

requirements.text: drive the load relay via GPIO12 with HA-controllable state
publish AC power metering (voltage / current / power / energy)
expose the front button as a binary_sensor + the status LED
ESPHome logger must NOT use UART0 because GPIO3 (RX) is wired to the CSE7766 stream

smart-plug-v1.description: ESP8285 1MB module with the older HLW8012 / BL0937 power-meter chip -- three pulse outputs (SEL drives the chip's mode, CF + CF1 carry the pulse rates back to the MCU). temp-above-turns-on-fan.description: Phase-4 worked example for intent-to-device synthesis: a BME280's temperature channel fires `on_value_range` with `above: 28.0`, and the action turns a fan on. Demonstrates the threshold-bounds path -- the trigger carries `above` (and optionally `below`), the lowering wraps the action list in a `{above, below, then}` range entry, and the rendered `on_value_range:` lands inside the `temperature:` sub-block (proving the channel + range surfaces compose). The threshold-only case (no `below`) is open-ended on the upper bound -- fires whenever the reading is at or above 28°C.
temp-above-turns-on-fan.name: Fan turns on above a temperature threshold

requirements.text: turn on the fan when temperature rises above 28C

temp-turns-on-fan.description: Phase-3 worked example for intent-to-device synthesis: a BME280's temperature channel triggers a switch action when its on_value fires. Exercises the multi-channel sensor trigger path -- the trigger carries a `channel: temperature` selector that the lowering combines with the event to land `on_value:` inside the `temperature:` sub-block (vs. the bme280's humidity / pressure siblings, which stay clear). Complements the single-channel sensor examples by proving the lowering picks the right sub-block on a multi-output sensor.
temp-turns-on-fan.name: Temperature turns on the fan

requirements.text: turn on the fan when temperature rises
